mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in PAYEMS (labor force employment) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to elevated corporate earnings growth and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where PAYEMS shows a positive month-over-month change (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 4.5% (indicating a restrictive monetary policy stance), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to heightened risk aversion and reduced liquidity in equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 198) and restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) signals an environment of persistent inflation and tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to increased risk of central bank rate hikes and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months meeting both CPIAUCSL > 198 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it signals an economic slowdown that triggers Federal Reserve rate-cutting cycles, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as equity valuations expand on lower discount rates and improved risk sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where UNRATE > 5.0% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in HOUST (housing starts) indicates strengthening demand for residential construction, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to elevated consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where HOUST shows a positive month-over-month change (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0 (indicating a contraction in manufacturing and services), it signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to reduced corporate earnings and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months where INDPRO < 105.0 (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate < 1.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 198) signals a stagflationary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to deteriorating corporate margins and increased policy uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters meeting both GDPC1 < 1.0% and CPIAUCSL > 198 (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 198) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%), the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to elevated interest rates and reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months meeting both CPIAUCSL > 198 and UNRATE < 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test against baseline).
